summary: Sung Bae Park is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Lewis Lancaster (~1974-1979). He served as an assistant professor at Dongguk University (~1970-1972) and held a post at Stony Brook University from 1977.

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, served as Director at Geumgang University, and became a professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
Sungtaek Cho works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Stony Brook University and served as Director at Korea University (attested 2012-2013).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the doctoral supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, London, and Paris. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1914-1952) and served as National Professor in Humanities (~1965-1977).
Surama Dasgupta was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed an M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta and a Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Tribhuvan University, supervised by Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervised by Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who earned PhDs from the universities of Calcutta and Cambridge. He lectured at Cambridge (~1920-1922), served as Principal of Sanskrit College (~1931-1942), and held the Philosophy Chair at Calcutta (~1942-1945).

Suryya Kumar Bhuyan was an Indologist and historian who studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta (~1913-1916). He later served as a professor at Cotton University (attested 1956).
Susan Andrews is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned her PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Chun-fang Yu.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, where she studied under Stephanie W. Jamison and other faculty.

Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history/archaeology who served on the faculty at Ohio State University from ~1971 to 2011, where she was a professor from ~1980 to 2011.
Susan Naquin is a historian and Sinologist who held posts at the University of Pennsylvania as a professor (~1976-1993) and at Princeton University (~1993-2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held academic posts at Yale (~1989-1996) and Tel Aviv University (~1996-2000), and joined the Einstein Forum around 2000.
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served on the faculty in the religion department at Amherst College from ~1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies who studied at SOAS. She directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993-2017) and held a post at the University of East Anglia (~2018).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph was an Indology scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She held academic posts at Harvard (~1954-1964) and the University of Chicago (~1964-2002).

Susanne Mrozik is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an M.T.S. at Harvard and completed her doctorate under Charles Hallisey. She held posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Visva-Bharati University. He served as a lecturer there in 1986 and as Lecturer in Indian Religions at the University of Birmingham.

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993-2001) under Makio Takemura. He has held part-time lecturer posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Hanazono University.
